response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack software engineer (15+ years) with strong web, backend, and some low-latency systems work, but the resume shows no evidence of SoC/IP modeling, hardware architecture, AI accelerator or GPU workload analysis, or deep-learning optimization — the core requirements of this Principal Performance Architect role. Education is a BS in Computer Science with sufficient years of experience to meet the formal bar, but the domain experience is essentially absent. Adjacent signals (C/C++ at National Instruments, embedded/robotics work at Altom, low-latency D services at Sociomantic) are the only partial matches and are dated or shallow relative to a principal-level hardware performance role.
strengths: 15+ years of broad software engineering experience, meeting the BS + 8 years bar
Some low-level/systems exposure: C/C++ at National Instruments, async low-latency services, embedded/robotics work
Strong engineering practices (TDD, CI/CD, tooling) and demonstrated community/teaching leadership
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, RTL, or hardware architecture experience whatsoever
No deep-learning workload, GPU, SIMD/MIMD, or AI accelerator performance analysis background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack, not principal-level hardware-software co-design

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture experience
No AI accelerator / GPU / deep-learning performance expertise
Meets formal education + years-of-experience requirement with some systems/C++ exposure
